data.severity: medium; 11 of 16 applicable scenarios have complete evidence, with five known gaps across malformed TOML, full precedence, enum/unsupported-option breadth, and platform/install behavior
data.impact_scope: Potentially affects users with malformed or layered configuration, untested enum or unsupported-option cases, Linux/WSL paths, and sample-copy installation workflows; executed evidence is limited to Windows local loopback mock behavior
data.estimated_repair_time: Approximately 0.5–1 working day for automatable configuration and option checks; Linux/WSL and installation-copy verification time is unknown pending environment and workflow availability
data.delivery_impact: Does not block transition to independent Reviewer because the same gaps were explicitly accepted as exceptions in the prior PM decision and this report shows no behavior failures; if release scope requires Linux/WSL or real installation-path evidence, supplement before release, with timing dependent on environment availability
data.rationale: The current event-bound Tester report records 19 of 19 behavior tests passed, zero failures, and the repaired TOML table-header comment behavior covered by S16. Five scenarios remain incomplete and branch coverage was not measured. These are transparent bounded evidence gaps, with no newly reported failure; they warrant continued visibility and possible release-stage verification but do not require blocking Reviewer handoff.
data.residual_risk: Malformed TOML handling, complete default/install/profile/CLI precedence, every enum, all unsupported flags, cross-platform paths, actual copy/no-overwrite behavior, real API behavior, and model availability remain unverified; branch coverage is unavailable.
data.uncertainty: Static review only; no commands run and coverage not independently recalculated. Installation workflow, Linux/WSL environment availability, and release scope are unspecified, so effort and release impact cannot be precise.
